data: {"type":"agent_chunk","agent":"synthesizer","content":"## How it works

CRISPR gene editing modifies the genomes of living organisms. A Cas9 nuclease is paired with a synthetic guide RNA (gRNA) and delivered into a cell, which cuts the genome at the desired location [1]. These programmable "molecular scissors" create double-strand breaks, allowing DNA to be inserted, deleted, modified, or replaced at specific sites [3].

## Natural origin

The technique is based on a simplified version of the bacterial CRISPR-Cas9 antiviral defense system [1]. In bacteria and archaea, CRISPR sequences derive from phage DNA and are used to detect and destroy similar phage DNA during later infections [2].

## Where it is used

The research confirms that CRISPR modifies genomes [1] but names no specific applications. A 2021 headline claims the technology opens the door to treating a broad array of diseases [4]. That is a headline, not clinical evidence, and the mechanistic sources do not support it.

## Gaps in the evidence

- The mechanism and bacterial-origin claims each rest on a single source. Corroborate them before relying on them.
- The research says nothing about off-target cuts, delivery into patient cells, or safety. These bear directly on any therapeutic claim.
- Treat the disease-treatment claim as unsupported until a peer-reviewed clinical source is added.

### Sources

1. [CRISPR gene editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR_gene_editing) - Wikipedia
2. [CRISPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRISPR) - Wikipedia
3. [Genome editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome_editing) - Wikipedia
4. [CRISPR gene-editing breakthrough opens door to treating broad array of diseases](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=27643517) - Hacker News, 600 points, 234 comments, Jun 2021
5. [HIV in cell culture can be completely eliminated using CRISPR-Cas gene editing (pdf)](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=39761283) - Hacker News, 324 points, 77 comments, Mar 2024
"}
